description: Model provider verification and models, the Claude Agent SDK status and update, custom providers, tier routing and the usage ledger (limits, summary, resolve, record, rate-limit snapshot, turn composition). Roster: all 14 method-paths below are in ALL_ENDPOINTS (extension/server.mjs), handled by extension/routes/router.mjs (the /kb/providers/*, /kb/agent-sdk*, /kb/custom-providers, /kb/routing-tiers and /kb/usage/* branches) and extension/server/tier-routing.mjs / custom-providers.mjs / providers/tier-routing.mjs / kb/usage.mjs. All are token-protected and on the core feature set. Request parts list exactly the keys each handler reads; every JSON route also answers a malformed body 400 (not declared, per SCHEMA.md). Rate limits: POST /kb/providers/verify and /kb/providers/models share llmFast (429 declared); POST /kb/usage/record and PUT /kb/usage/limits share kbWrite (429 declared). POST /kb/agent-sdk/update has no request body. Not captured: the Claude SDK model listing (needs the local Claude CLI login), an ok:true verify (a live provider listing), an install through POST /kb/agent-sdk/update, and an Anthropic rate-limit snapshot; the schema says so where it matters, and x-optional marks the unfixtured properties. The two Agent SDK fixtures are produced in-process by calling llm_agent/sdk/updater.mjs (its registry fetch stubbed offline, the install refused) because the route itself would reach the npm registry; the bodies are the functions' return values, which the route sends verbatim.

Resolution.description: The resolver verdict (kb/usage.mjs resolveModel). used, limit, pct and unit are present only when a model was picked (ok or degraded); a paused or unconfigured verdict has no pick.

resetAt.description: ISO-8601 window reset; null when there is no chain

provider.description: anthropic | openai | google | deepseek | jev | custom:<id>

body.description: provider is required (an unknown or empty one answers 400). mode 'cli' checks the provider's CLI binary; any other value is the key mode. apiKey, when absent, is the stored key. baseUrl is read only for provider custom.

apiKey.description: placeholder in fixtures; never a real key

200.description: Always 200 unless the request is invalid. ok true is answered only after a live model listing, which the capture does not reach (no external network); the true shape is the same.

The live chat models for a provider, or [] with a detail. entries and source are the Claude SDK variant (anthropic only, server API v57+ / v63+): entries carries display names and effort levels. The SDK variant is not captured (it needs the local Claude CLI login), so entries and source are optional and not covered by a fixture.

detail.description: Human-readable reason when models is empty

entries.description: anthropic via the Agent SDK only

source.description: Present when the list came from the Agent SDK

200.description: Claude Agent SDK version status (llm_agent/sdk/updater.mjs sdkStatus). The 200 fixture is produced in-process with an offline registry stub; the route itself reads the npm registry.

error.description: Why the registry could not be checked

200.description: Always 200: ok says whether the SDK was updated; a refusal or rollback is a normal answer. The 200 fixture is a refusal (a chat turn running), produced in-process; an install would run npm in the server checkout and reach the registry, so no install is captured.

items.description: A custom provider as the Mac app sends it (Core/Platform/CustomProvider.swift). The server keeps id, name, baseURL, models, isOpenAICompatible, isEnabled and anthropicBaseURL; apiKey is the vault key path (for example custom.<id>.apiKey), never the key itself. Invalid entries (no http(s) baseURL, no name) are dropped; at most 50 are stored.

anthropicBaseURL.description: Anthropic-format endpoint for the Agent engine; null when absent

200.description: The stored tier routing (tiers, features) plus each tier's usability by the server's own resolver (status) and each configured role's (featureStatus). A keyless openai or google tier answers after a short CLI health probe.

provider.description: anthropic | openai | google | deepseek | jev | custom:<id>

reason.description: unset | not_found | disabled | no_key | no_key_or_cli (OpenAI/Google, v68+) | cli_unverified (CLI health probe not run yet, v69+) | cli_failed / route_failed (the route failed at runtime in the last ~10 min, v69+) | error (only when usable is false)

agentReason.description: why the Agent engine cannot run a usable tier, e.g. not_agent_capable

via.description: API v68+, only when usable. `key` = runs on an API key (user vault or operator env; custom providers always), `cli` = runs on the provider's logged-in CLI subscription (claude / codex / gemini). A key wins when both exist.

status.description: Keys: configured tiers, plus unset ones (reason unset) when a tier is absent.

reason.description: set when unusable: a tier reason, cli_untrusted_input, or decision_only

featureStatus.description: API v69+. One entry per CONFIGURED feature. `usable: false` with the tier's own reason when the tier is unusable, or `cli_untrusted_input` when the tier runs on a keyless codex/gemini CLI and the feature is `internal` or `pipeline` (untrusted email/connector/transcript input; pipeline output is dispatched to issue trackers), or `decision_only` (API v73+) when the tier runs on `jev` and the feature is anything but `decisions`.

body.description: The whole routing table; the server replaces the user's table. Invalid entries are dropped, not rejected (see dropped). A body that is not a JSON object answers 400 (no type is declared so that refusal can be exemplified).

provider.description: anthropic | openai | google | deepseek | jev | custom:<id>

features.description: Keys subagents | loop | autoTasks | quickChat | pipeline | internal | decisions (API v73+); values a tier name

dropped.description: Entries that were not stored (API v67+)

provider.description: anthropic | openai | google | custom; restricts chains to that provider

chains.description: Per provider, the chain of models with their caps. GET lists the built-in chain merged with the user's overrides, sorted by priority.

body.description: chains is required (400 otherwise). Only the providers present are replaced. Each entry reads model, priority, enabled, limit_value, unit, window_kind and threshold_pct; the server ignores the read-only label and custom the Mac also sends.

chains.description: { provider: [ { model, priority, enabled, limit_value, unit, window_kind, threshold_pct } ] }
Per provider, the chain of models with their caps. GET lists the built-in chain merged with the user's overrides, sorted by priority.

active.description: The resolver verdict (kb/usage.mjs resolveModel). used, limit, pct and unit are present only when a model was picked (ok or degraded); a paused or unconfigured verdict has no pick.

resetAt.description: ISO-8601 window reset; null when there is no chain

provider.description: anthropic | openai | google | custom; default anthropic

prefer.description: the caller's desired model, kept when healthy

ratelimits.description: The latest Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible rate-limit snapshot from a live response's headers (in-memory, per server run). null when only the CLI path ran, which is always the case offline. The object shape (capturedAt, provider, model, requests, tokens, inputTokens, outputTokens; each bucket limit/remaining/reset) is described but not covered: no live response is captured.

limit.description: 1-200, default 50 Clamped to 1-200; the default is 50.

items.description: One row of turn_composition (migration 0040, 0044), columns camelCased, user_id and id omitted. *Tokens are chars/4 estimates of LLM-IDE text; sdk* are the SDK's own end-of-turn categories. sdkCategories is a 'name:kind=tokens;...' string. resumed is 0 or 1.

body.description: Read by POST /kb/usage/record. provider and model are required (400 otherwise). Token and turn counts are optional non-negative integers; absent or null means not reported. source is api | cli | auto-task (any other value is stored as api).

200.description: ok is false and id null when the ledger write failed (best effort).
